"Just so is it, venerable sir, as you say. / I indeed approach you [as a pupil]." / "If you had not spoken thus, your head would have flown apart. / Come, then, I will tell you that so that it will not fly apart. / When one who knows thus eats and drinks, speech is satisfied thereby. / Speech being satisfied, fire is satisfied. / Fire being satisfied, the earth is satisfied. / The earth being satisfied, whatever beings are attached to the earth are satisfied. / When one who knows thus eats and drinks, the breath is satisfied thereby. / The breath being satisfied, the wind is satisfied. / The wind being satisfied, the intermediate space is satisfied. / The intermediate space being satisfied, whatever beings are attached to the intermediate space are satisfied. / When one who knows thus eats and drinks, the eye is satisfied thereby. / The eye being satisfied, the sun is satisfied. / The sun being satisfied, heaven is satisfied. / Heaven being satisfied, whatever beings are attached to heaven are satisfied. / When one who knows thus eats and drinks, the mind is satisfied thereby. / The mind being satisfied, the moon is satisfied. / The moon being satisfied, the waters are satisfied. / The waters being satisfied, whatever beings are attached to the waters are satisfied. / When one who knows thus eats and drinks, hearing is satisfied thereby. / Hearing being satisfied, the quarters and intermediate regions are satisfied. / The quarters and intermediate regions being satisfied, whatever beings are attached to the quarters and intermediate regions are satisfied."

For him who knows thus, eating and drinking, this right hand is the offering spoon juhū;

1.3.15.s: priyamedhā ha vai bharadvājā yajñavido manyamānās te ha sma na kañ cana vedavidam upayanti te sarvam avidus te sahaivāvidus te 'gnihotra eva na samavadanta teṣām ekaḥ sakṛd agnihotram ajuhod dvir ekas trir ekas teṣāṃ yaḥ sakṛd agnihotram ajuhot tam itarāv apṛcchatāṃ kasmai tvaṃ juhoṣīti ekadhā vā idaṃ sarvaṃ prajāpatiḥ prajāpataya evāhaṃ sāyaṃ juhomīti prajāpataye prātar iti teṣāṃ yo dvir ajuhot tam itarāv apṛcchatāṃ kābhyāṃ tvaṃ juhoṣīti agnaye prajāpataya iti sāyaṃ sūryāya prajāpataya iti prātas teṣāṃ yas trir ajuhot tam itarāv apṛcchatāṃ kebhyas tvaṃ juhoṣīty agnaye prajāpataye 'numataya iti sāyaṃ sūryāya prajāpataye 'gnaye sviṣṭakṛta iti prātas teṣāṃ yo dvir ajuhot sa ārdhnot sa bhūyiṣṭho 'bhavat prajayā cetarau śriyā cetarāv atyākrāmat tasya ha prajām itarayoḥ praje sajātatvam upaitām tasmād dvir hotavyaṃ yajuṣā caiva manasā ca yām eva sa ṛddhim ārdhnot tām ṛdhnoti ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān agnihotraṃ juhotīti brāhmaṇam ||
1.3.15.d: प्रियमेधा ह वै भरद्वाजा यज्ञविदो मन्यमानास् ते ह स्म न कञ् चन वेदविदम् उपयन्ति ते सर्वम् अविदुस् ते सहैवाविदुस् ते ऽग्निहोत्र एव न समवदन्त तेषाम् एकः सकृद् अग्निहोत्रम् अजुहोद् द्विर् एकस् त्रिर् एकस् तेषां यः सकृद् अग्निहोत्रम् अजुहोत् तम् इतराव् अपृच्छतां कस्मै त्वं जुहोषीति एकधा वा इदं सर्वं प्रजापतिः प्रजापतय एवाहं सायं जुहोमीति प्रजापतये प्रातर् इति तेषां यो द्विर् अजुहोत् तम् इतराव् अपृच्छतां काभ्यां त्वं जुहोषीति अग्नये प्रजापतय इति सायं सूर्याय प्रजापतय इति प्रातस् तेषां यस् त्रिर् अजुहोत् तम् इतराव् अपृच्छतां केभ्यस् त्वं जुहोषीत्य् अग्नये प्रजापतये ऽनुमतय इति सायं सूर्याय प्रजापतये ऽग्नये स्विष्टकृत इति प्रातस् तेषां यो द्विर् अजुहोत् स आर्ध्नोत् स भूयिष्ठो ऽभवत् प्रजया चेतरौ श्रिया चेतराव् अत्याक्रामत् तस्य ह प्रजाम् इतरयोः प्रजे सजातत्वम् उपैताम् तस्माद् द्विर् होतव्यं यजुषा चैव मनसा च याम् एव स ऋद्धिम् आर्ध्नोत् ताम् ऋध्नोति य एवं वेद यश् चैवंविद्वान् अग्निहोत्रं जुहोतीति ब्राह्मणम् ॥
1.3.15.m:
Ever sacrificed, ever offered, ever eaten and drunk is the Agnihotra of him who knows thus and who, knowing thus, offers the Agnihotra; thus the Brāhmaṇa.

The Priyamedha Bharadvājas, indeed, thinking themselves to be knowers of sacrifice,
would not approach any knower of the Veda.
They knew everything;
they knew [it] together.
They disagreed only regarding the Agnihotra.
One of them offered the Agnihotra once, one twice, one thrice.
To the one among them who offered the Agnihotra once, the other two said: 'To whom do you offer?'
'Prajāpati is indeed this whole [universe] in one way.
I offer to Prajāpati alone in the evening; to Prajāpati in the morning.'
To the one among them who offered twice, the other two said: 'To whom [two] do you offer?'
'To Agni [and] Prajāpati in the evening; to Sūrya [and] Prajāpati in the morning.'
To the one among them who offered thrice, the other two said: 'To whom [pl.] do you offer?' 'To Agni, Prajāpati, and Anumati in the evening; to Sūrya, Prajāpati, and Agni Sviṣṭakṛt in the morning.'
The one among them who offered twice prospered;
he became the greatest;
he surpassed the other two in offspring and fortune.
The offspring of the other two entered into the status of kinship [as dependents] to his offspring.
Therefore, one should offer twice, with a yajus-formula and silently in mind.
He prospers with the very prosperity with which that one prospered, who knows thus and who, knowing thus, offers the Agnihotra. Such is the Brāhmaṇa. || 15

1.3.16.s: svāhā vai kutaḥ saṃbhūtā kena prakṛtā kiṃ vāsyā gotram katy akṣarā kati padā kati varṇā kiṃ pūrvāvasānā kva cit sthitā kim adhiṣṭhānā brūhi svāhāyā yad daivataṃ rūpaṃ ca svāhā vai satyasaṃbhūtā brahmaṇā prakṛtā lāmagāyanasagotrā dve akṣare ekaṃ padam trayaś ca varṇāḥ śuklaḥ padmaḥ suvarṇa iti sarvacchandasāṃ vedeṣu samāsabhūtaikocchvāsā varṇānte catvāro vedāḥ śarīre ṣaḍaṅgāny oṣadhivanaspatayo lomāni cakṣuṣī sūryācandramasau sā svāhā sā svadhā yajñeṣu vaṣaṭkārabhūtā prayujyate tasyā agnir daivatam brāhmaṇo rūpam iti brāhmaṇam ||
1.3.16.d: स्वाहा वै कुतः संभूता केन प्रकृता किं वास्या गोत्रम् कत्य् अक्षरा कति पदा कति वर्णा किं पूर्वावसाना क्व चित् स्थिता किम् अधिष्ठाना ब्रूहि स्वाहाया यद् दैवतं रूपं च स्वाहा वै सत्यसंभूता ब्रह्मणा प्रकृता लामगायनसगोत्रा द्वे अक्षरे एकं पदम् त्रयश् च वर्णाः शुक्लः पद्मः सुवर्ण इति सर्वच्छन्दसां वेदेषु समासभूतैकोच्छ्वासा वर्णान्ते चत्वारो वेदाः शरीरे षडङ्गान्य् ओषधिवनस्पतयो लोमानि चक्षुषी सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ सा स्वाहा सा स्वधा यज्ञेषु वषट्कारभूता प्रयुज्यते तस्या अग्निर् दैवतम् ब्राह्मणो रूपम् इति ब्राह्मणम् ॥
1.3.16.m:
From what, indeed, did Svāhā arise?
By whom was she produced?
What is her lineage?
How many syllables [has she]?
How many words?
How many colours?
What are her initial and final [elements]?
Where does she abide?
What is her support?
Declare what is the deity and the form of Svāhā!
Svāhā arose from Truth;
she was produced by Brahman;
she belongs to the Lāmagāyana lineage;
[she has] two syllables,
one word,
and three colours: white, lotus-red, and golden.
She is the condensation of all metres in the Vedas, [uttered in] a single breath; at the end of the sound, the four Vedas are in [her] body;
the six auxiliary disciplines [are her limbs]; the herbs and forest trees are her body-hairs;
her two eyes are the sun and the moon.
She, as Svāhā, as Svadhā, is employed in the sacrifices, having become the vaṣaṭ-call.
Agni is her deity;
a brāhmaṇa is her form. Such is the Brāhmaṇa. || 16

1.3.17.s: athāpi kāravo ha nāma ṛṣayo 'lpasvā āsan ta imam ekagum agniṣṭomaṃ dadṛśus tam āharan tenāyajanta te svar yayuḥ sa ya icchet svar iyām iti sa etenaikagunāgniṣṭomena yajeteti brāhmaṇam ||
1.3.17.d: अथापि कारवो ह नाम ऋषयो ऽल्पस्वा आसन् त इमम् एकगुम् अग्निष्टोमं ददृशुस् तम् आहरन् तेनायजन्त ते स्वर् ययुः स य इच्छेत् स्वर् इयाम् इति स एतेनैकगुनाग्निष्टोमेन यजेतेति ब्राह्मणम् ॥
